coordinateNote: All coordinates are selenographic (latitude/longitude) in the MOON_ME (Mean Earth) body-fixed frame unless otherwise noted. Coordinates are sourced from published mission reports, NASA/ESA documentation, and LROC/LOLA data. Some coordinates are approximate centroids of landing ellipses.

sites.name: Shackleton Rim
sites.description: Rim of Shackleton crater near the lunar south pole. One of the Artemis III candidate landing regions. Receives near-continuous illumination due to its elevated position.
sites.source: NASA Artemis III candidate landing regions (2022); de Rosa et al. 2012, Icarus 221(2)

sites.name: Malapert Massif
sites.description: A prominent mountain near the lunar south pole. Candidate Artemis III landing region with favorable illumination and line-of-sight to Earth.
sites.source: NASA Artemis III candidate landing regions (2022); Zuber et al. 2012, Nature 486

sites.name: Nobile Rim
sites.description: Western rim of Nobile crater near the south pole. Was selected as the VIPER rover landing site. Contains permanently shadowed regions nearby.
sites.source: NASA VIPER site selection (2021); Colaprete et al.

sites.name: Haworth Crater Rim
sites.description: Rim of Haworth crater near the south pole. Interior contains permanently shadowed regions of scientific interest.
sites.source: NASA Artemis III candidate landing regions; Mazarico et al. 2011, Icarus 211

sites.name: IM-1 Malapert A
sites.description: Landing site of the Odysseus lander (IM-1 mission) near Malapert A crater. First commercial lunar landing, 22 Feb 2024.
sites.source: Intuitive Machines IM-1 mission data (2024); NASA CLPS

sites.name: Chandrayaan-3 (Shiv Shakti Point)
sites.description: Landing site of India's Chandrayaan-3 Vikram lander, 23 Aug 2023. Southernmost successful soft landing at the time.
sites.source: ISRO Chandrayaan-3 mission data (2023); LROC imaging

sites.name: Chang'e 4 (Von Kármán)
sites.description: First-ever soft landing on the lunar far side, in Von Kármán crater, 3 Jan 2019.
sites.source: CNSA Chang'e 4 mission data (2019); Huang et al. 2018, JGR Planets

sites.name: Chang'e 6 (Apollo Basin)
sites.description: First sample return from the lunar far side, in Apollo crater, June 2024.

sites.name: Apollo 11 — Tranquility Base
sites.description: First human landing on the Moon, 20 July 1969. Sea of Tranquility (Mare Tranquillitatis).
sites.source: NASA Apollo 11 mission report; LROC NAC imaging; Wagner et al. 2017

sites.name: Apollo 15 — Hadley–Apennine
sites.description: Apollo 15 landing at the Hadley-Apennine region, 30 July 1971. Near Hadley Rille.
sites.source: NASA Apollo 15 mission report; LROC NAC imaging

sites.name: Apollo 17 — Taurus–Littrow
sites.description: Last crewed lunar landing, 11 December 1972. Taurus-Littrow valley.
sites.source: NASA Apollo 17 mission report; LROC NAC imaging

sites.name: Connecting Ridge
sites.description: Ridge connecting Shackleton and de Gerlache craters. Extended illumination periods and potential volatile access.
sites.source: NASA Artemis III candidate landing regions (2022)

sites.name: de Gerlache Rim
sites.description: Rim of de Gerlache crater near the south pole. Elevated terrain with favorable illumination.
sites.source: NASA Artemis III candidate landing regions (2022); Bussey et al. 2010
